design_decisions.decision: Startup: inner coroutine _load_state_unbounded + thin wait_for wrapper, rather than indenting the body; TimeoutError from queries re-raised in the inner handler so only one fixed-text line is logged.
ping() bounded both inside (wait_for) and in the router (wait_for), so FakeDatabase hangs are bounded too.
Request-timeout tests use httpx ASGITransport with outer asyncio.wait_for (rather than sync TestClient) so a regression fails instead of hanging.

Pre-existing client_no_db fixture injects a fake upstream, so its /health is database disabled, upstream disconnected, degraded (spec criterion 3 said upstream disabled; tested the no-upstream variant separately via factory returning None).

implementation.deviations: Only criterion 3 wording (above). Health router returns JSONResponse instead of a response model. Routers unchanged. Stray scratchpad PG data dir deleted; no process left.
implementation.claude_md_text: API: "GET /health is open (no key) and returns {status, database, upstream}; database ok|down|disabled (disabled = RULES_PERSISTENCE_ENABLED=false), upstream connected|disconnected|disabled (disabled = no Finnhub key); HTTP 503 only when database is down." Invariant 5: "Every database operation is time-bounded by constants in db.py: DB_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (5), DB_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (5), DB_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (30; startup fails loudly with 'startup failed: ... timed out'), HEALTH_DB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (2); a timeout in a request path is a 503, in a writer a failed write." Also: test doubles' acquire() must accept timeout=; remove any "/health is plain liveness" statement.
implementation.self_critique: Real-PG lock test proves command_timeout surfaces as 503 for rules/alerts; acquire timeout against real asyncpg is only covered with stubs. Startup timeout covered with fakes only, not a real hung Postgres.
